entrypoints.summary: An actor with Batch RegisterJobDefinition and SubmitJob permission registers a container job definition whose command queries EC2 IMDSv2, then submits it to the EC2 Batch queue.
POST /ns-command passes caller-controlled domain_name into a shell command submitted as a Fargate Batch command override; this is distinct from the EC2 metadata-boundary mechanism.

affected_components.role: Grants ecs-role Batch registration/submission and broad S3 permissions.
Defines EC2 compute and assigns ecs-role to the EC2 job definition.
Separate HTTP-to-Batch command override and job-log observation path.

causal_paths.kind: Batch job-definition registration to host metadata credential retrieval

observability.positive_marker: The writeup shows a collaborator POST containing an EC2 role ARN and temporary credentials.

preconditions: An EC2-orchestrated AWS Batch compute environment is used.
The actor has batch:RegisterJobDefinition and batch:SubmitJob.
The container can reach EC2 IMDSv2.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Shell command in Batch container properties sends IMDS output externally.
trigger_steps.summary: Register a container job definition that requests an IMDSv2 token and instance-role credentials.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: SubmitJob specifies the attacker-controlled definition and LowPriorityEc2.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit that definition to the EC2 Batch queue.

mitigations.concept: Block job-container access to EC2 instance metadata service
Remove Batch job-definition registration and submission authority from job-accessible roles

sources.concept: AWS IAM policy granting Batch RegisterJobDefinition and SubmitJob

impact.affected_asset: AWS IAM permissions and cloud resources accessible to the EC2 Spot instance role.
impact.attacker_capability: Obtain and use EC2 IMDS credentials after registering and submitting an attacker-controlled job.
impact.security_effect: Cloud privilege escalation through exposure of host EC2 instance-role temporary credentials to a Batch job container.

causal_trace.summary: The lab ecs-role policy grants batch:RegisterJobDefinition and batch:SubmitJob on wildcard resources.
EC2-orchestrated Batch job containers can reach the host instance metadata service while an actor can control a registered and submitted container command.
The demonstrated job command obtains an IMDSv2 token and requests host instance-role credentials from 169.254.169.254.
The writeup reports receipt of EC2 Spot instance-role credentials and access to other tenants' data.

failure.operation: Container-originated EC2 IMDSv2 retrieval of host instance-role credentials

primary_invariant.statement: A Batch job submitter or compromised job container must not gain host EC2 instance-role credentials by controlling a job definition and command.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The writeup states EC2-orchestrated Batch jobs share a network interface with the EC2 Spot instance IMDS, and the policy grants registration and submission of attacker-controlled jobs.

quality.review_notes: The writeup includes a reported collaborator receipt of instance-role credentials and the pinned lab contains matching Batch/IAM configuration, but no execution result from the pinned lab is provided. The Fargate HTTP shell-interpolation path is separate from the EC2 IMDS mechanism. No source-specific hardened policy diff is present.

remediation.invariant_restored: Jobs cannot access host metadata credentials, and job-accessible roles cannot register and submit uncontrolled job definitions.
mitigation_classes: network restriction of instance metadata service from jobs

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The demonstrated actor requires Batch job-definition registration and submission permissions.
data_structure_invariants: Job-container network access must not provide host instance-role credentials.
Job-accessible roles must not retain unrestricted job-definition control-plane authority.
state_context.state_machine: Register attacker-controlled job definition; submit to EC2 queue; run on EC2; query IMDSv2; exfiltrate credential response.

target.component: AWS Batch EC2 compute environment and job-definition/control-plane permissions
